output.summary: Herbaceous perennial native to Western Europe, North Africa and Asia. It has showy mauve-purple flowers with dark veins and commonly grows in meadows, hedgerows and fallow fields. Young leaves and shoots are eaten raw or cooked and have a long history as wild food.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves and shoots are eaten raw or cooked; boiled young leaves were used as a vegetable in parts of 19th-century Europe.
